truths.truth: verify.md states the human-check bar explicitly - human-verify only when the model cannot execute (irreversible against real data, or outside reach: credentials, GUI, hardware, another machine)
truths.evidence: cadence-core/workflows/verify.md:141-146 - '**The bar.** An item is a HUMAN check only when the model cannot execute it - it is irreversible against real data, or it is outside the model's reach (credentials it does not hold, a GUI, hardware, another machine). Everything else the model runs.' Matches item 1's `expected` verbatim in wording and in the four named exclusions.

truths.truth: The bar's operational predicate admits ONLY items the model cannot execute - i.e. the two 'already judged' short-circuits are true supersets of nothing model-executable
truths.evidence: cadence-core/workflows/verify.md:147-153 routes an item carrying `why_human` straight to pass 2, 'their reason stands and is not re-litigated'. But `skills/cad-verifier-contract/SKILL.md:194` writes `human_checks` (and therefore `why_human`) 'one per UNCERTAIN truth and per human-only check', and :86-90 creates UNCERTAIN whenever a wired truth simply lacks an observed probe ('Upgrade to VERIFIED only on evidence - one named test that exercises it passes... Otherwise the truth is UNCERTAIN and becomes a human check'). A truth whose only defect is that the verifier did not run the named test is exactly a model-executable check, and it arrives at the walk carrying `why_human`. The SUMMARY's third high finding is confirmed against both files.

truths.truth: A model-executed UAT result is mechanically distinguishable from a user answer and from a deep-pass verifier result, and `why_human` survives merge into UAT.md
truths.evidence: cadence-core/bin/lib/planning-files.mjs:954 `UAT_SOURCES = ['user','verifier','model']`, :942 `why_human` registered in UAT_FIELDS; cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs:561-562 pre-write enum guard, :597 `if (source !== 'user') item.source = source` (user stays implicit), :765-773 merge carries `why_human`. Four named tests pass: planning.test.mjs:857, :871, :882, :895 (full run 1367 pass / 0 fail).

truths.truth: A live walk over 9 read-only items + 1 destructive item ends the turn asking about exactly 1 item, with a 9-row executed-and-cited table above it
truths.evidence: The prose exists (cadence-core/workflows/verify.md:139-200 pass 1 / pass 2, report line at :321 `{v} auto-verified, {m} model-executed`), but the walk is only reachable through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` resolution in skills/cad-verify, so no probe in this tree observes the turn-ending behaviour. Compounded by truth 2: the `why_human` short-circuit would send model-executable items to the ask even after a reinstall.

truths.truth: The one-re-arm cap is stated in one place every risk_surface fire site shares, and reaches all five sites
truths.evidence: The cap itself is real and terminal: cadence-core/references/triage-gate.md:14-32 ('**The blocking re-arm is capped at ONE round.**', narrowed second pass, terminal ask naming '`<trigger>` re-armed once on its own fix and still reports N blocker/high findings', 'never fire that trigger again in this loop'), with the /clear caveat stated at :29-32. Reach is the hole. Repo-wide grep for `triage-gate` outside the file itself returns 9 hits; every RE-READ imperative is scoped to a non-risk_surface arm: execute.md:265 (`diff` at adjudicated), :351 and :363 (`diff` / `phase_diff` at adjudicated), verify.md:259 (the fix-list adjudication), plan.md:248, skills/cad-land/SKILL.md:57. task.md:74, debug.md:110 and references/git-guard.md:121-122 name only `references/review-triggers.md`, whose step 6 (:187) delegates declaratively ('holds this step whole') with no read imperative. execute.md's own risk_surface handler at :282-289 restates the blocking consequence INLINE with no cap and no pointer ('Blocking: on FAIL, findings are fixed or the user explicitly overrides - never silently proceed'), and :267-269 actively steers the reader away ('The `risk_surface` arm is untouched by any of that'). execute.md:307-308 does name the cap, but in the worktree-remedy paragraph, not at the fire site.

truths.truth: /cad-audit FAILs on an already-published planning-doc version, fixture-proved, with the three non-drift states honored
truths.evidence: Seam: cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs:998-1008 computes `docVersion` -> `tagCarrying(readTags(dir), ...)` -> emits `version_drift {doc_version, published_as, cycle_state}`. Six fixtures on a tagged scratch repo, all green when run by name (planning.test.mjs:2044 drift fires, :2052 every-phase-complete exemption, :2062 sort-below is not drift, :2071 no-git-repo, :2085 ROADMAP-title fallback, :2096 the #87 v2.4.0 regression pin). Gate acts on it: audit.md:104-111 (the break), :121 (§3 remedy pair), :144 ('OR `version_drift` is present' inside FAIL), :152-170 (not-additive argument, the three non-drift states, the manifest-is-not-a-comparand argument).

truths.truth: The interrupted-close exemption exempts exactly the states audit.md declares exempt
truths.evidence: planning.mjs:1007-1008 gates the exemption on `derivePhases(...).some((p) => p.status !== 'complete')`, and planning.mjs:116-130 derives `complete` only when SUMMARY.md exists AND `uatComplete(uat)`; planning-files.mjs:1097-1099 makes `uatComplete` false for any item that is not pass-or-skipped-with-reason. Two consequences: (a) milestone.md:82-83 explicitly sanctions closing with an unfinished phase left in place ('a milestone can close with deferred work that rolls to the next'), so a close interrupted between the tag and the PROJECT.md evolve in that sanctioned shape fires drift in the state audit.md:159-161 calls exempt; (b) a UAT holding a `blocked` item can never derive complete, while verify.md:158 states `blocked` is TERMINAL ('nothing returns an item to the walk from it'), so audit.md:110-111's remedy 'complete the close so no phase is left open' is unreachable for that phase. The SUMMARY's second high finding is confirmed.

Working tree clean apart from the untracked UAT.md, so the committed weight-budgets.json is the one that passes (e8b949b and 50dca22 both carry budget updates). No unreferenced debt markers on the goal path: every TODO/placeholder hit in the changed files is parser test data or prose about comment grammar.

gaps.name: risk_surface re-arm is bounded
gaps.reason: unwired - the cap text is real and terminal, but no risk_surface fire site is instructed to load the file that holds it, and execute.md's fire site restates the blocking consequence inline without it
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/references/triage-gate.md:14-32 holds a correct, terminating cap with a named terminal ask. Reach fails: all nine external references to triage-gate.md are scoped to non-risk_surface arms - execute.md:265, :351, :363 (diff / phase_diff at adjudicated), verify.md:259 (fix-list adjudication), plan.md:248, skills/cad-land/SKILL.md:57. cadence-core/workflows/task.md:74, cadence-core/workflows/debug.md:110 and cadence-core/references/git-guard.md:121-122 point only at review-triggers.md, whose step 6 (references/review-triggers.md:187) delegates declaratively with no read imperative. cadence-core/workflows/execute.md:282-289 restates the blocking arm inline with no cap, and :267-269 tells the reader the risk_surface arm is 'untouched by any of that'. execute.md:307-308 names the cap only in the worktree-remedy paragraph.
gaps.missing: An explicit read/RE-READ of references/triage-gate.md at each risk_surface fire site (execute.md's handle_checkpoint risk_surface bullet, task.md risk_check, debug.md Resolve step 3, verify.md step 3's commit-time fire, git-guard.md §4), or a one-line cap restatement at the fire sites; plus turning review-triggers.md:187's 'holds this step whole' into a read imperative. Also fold the cap into execute.md:282-289's inline blocking restatement so it stops shadowing the shared file.

gaps.name: The walk's human-check bar admits model-executable items via why_human
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - verify.md's short-circuit treats why_human as proof an item is human-only, but the verifier contract writes why_human for every UNCERTAIN truth, including truths a model can settle by running a named test
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/workflows/verify.md:147-153 ('Two kinds of item are ALREADY judged; their reason stands and is not re-litigated... an item carrying `why_human` - the deep pass ruled on it and said why... Both go straight to pass 2, and pass 1 never runs their commands') against skills/cad-verifier-contract/SKILL.md:194 ('`human_checks` - one per UNCERTAIN truth and per human-only check') and :86-90 (a wired truth with no observed probe becomes UNCERTAIN and therefore a human check). The union is strictly larger than 'the model cannot execute it', so exactly the items FRI-01 exists to stop interrogating the user about can carry why_human and skip pass 1.
gaps.missing: Either narrow the contract so why_human is written only for human-only checks (a separate field, e.g. why_uncertain, for probe-less UNCERTAIN truths), or make verify.md re-apply the bar to a why_human item instead of treating it as already judged - read the reason and route to pass 2 only when it names irreversibility or an out-of-reach resource. Whichever side moves, the two files must state the same predicate.

gaps.name: version_drift's interrupted-close exemption fires on a sanctioned close
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the exemption is 'every phase derives complete', which is narrower than the state audit.md declares exempt, and its stated remedy is unreachable for a phase holding a blocked UAT item
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs:1007-1008 (`derivePhases(...).some((p) => p.status !== 'complete')`), :116-130 (complete requires SUMMARY.md AND uatComplete), cadence-core/bin/lib/planning-files.mjs:1097-1099 (a blocked item makes uatComplete false) against cadence-core/workflows/milestone.md:82-83 ('a milestone can close with deferred work that rolls to the next') and cadence-core/workflows/audit.md:159-161 (the exemption as written) plus audit.md:110-111 (the remedy) and cadence-core/workflows/verify.md:158 ('`blocked` is TERMINAL'). Not reproducible in this repo today because no tag carries the docs' Active version.
gaps.missing: Widen the exemption to the state milestone.md actually sanctions - e.g. exempt when the tag exists and no phase is still pre-SUMMARY, or exempt phases whose only incompleteness is a blocked/deferred UAT item - and add a fixture for the tag-plus-rolled-over-phase shape. If the narrow predicate is intended, restate audit.md:159-161 and the :110-111 remedy in those exact terms.

gaps.name: version_drift's comparand is a first-version-token scan of free prose
gaps.reason: behavior wrong under a benign edit - activeVersion() returns the first version token anywhere in the PROJECT.md ### Active body, so an Active section that names the predecessor before the current milestone reports the predecessor and hard-FAILs the ship gate on correct docs
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/lib/branch-decision.mjs:57-68 (scan from `### Active` to the next heading, return the first VERSION_RE match) feeding cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs:998. This repo's .planning/PROJECT.md:103 happens to name v2.6.0 before :104 names the closed v2.5.0, so the correct token wins today by ordering alone; one clause reorder inverts it, and v2.5.0 IS tagged.
gaps.missing: Anchor the comparand to the Active milestone's declared form (the bolded backticked `vX.Y.Z — name` token) rather than the first token in the body, or take the last/only token on the milestone-declaration line, with a fixture for an Active body that mentions the predecessor first.

human_checks.name: Reinstall the plugin from cadence/v2.6.0, build a scratch phase with 9 read-only-command UAT items + 1 destructive item, and run /cad-verify <N>
human_checks.expected: The turn ends asking about exactly 1 item, a 9-row executed-and-cited results table is printed above the ask, and `grep -c '^source: model' .planning/phases/<N>/UAT.md` returns 9. Steps: 1) reinstall the plugin from this branch; 2) create the scratch phase and its UAT.md; 3) run `/cad-verify <N>`; 4) run `grep -c '^source: model' .planning/phases/<N>/UAT.md` and expect `9`.
human_checks.why_human: The walk is prose the host resolves through ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}; nothing in this checkout executes it, so no probe here can observe whether the turn actually ends after one item. Note the why_human gap above predicts a failure mode for this check: any scratch item carrying why_human will route to the ask regardless of executability.

human_checks.name: With the plugin reinstalled, run /cad-audit against a checkout whose PROJECT.md ### Active names an already-tagged version
human_checks.expected: The gate reports FAIL and names the doc version, the tag spelling that carries it, and the cycle state - not a PASS-with-warnings. Steps: 1) reinstall the plugin from this branch; 2) point a scratch checkout's PROJECT.md ### Active at a version the repo already tags; 3) run `/cad-audit`; 4) expect a FAIL verdict citing version_drift.
human_checks.why_human: D-17: skills/cad-audit/SKILL.md:30 resolves the seam through ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, so the installed command still runs the previous plugin version. The seam and its fixtures are proven here; the end-to-end gate verdict is not observable from this branch.
